requirement: Reads plain <mzML> and <indexedmzML> files and returns the same spectra from both; the index is not used by the reader
Streams the file: each spectrum or chromatogram is yielded as soon as it ends and its element is freed so memory does not grow with the number of spectra
Decodes base64 binary arrays with no compression or zlib as 32-bit or 64-bit little-endian floats
Returns per spectrum: id, index, MS level, centroid or profile, scan start time and its unit, m/z and intensity arrays, total ion current
Returns precursor information for MS2 spectra: isolation window, selected ion m/z, charge, intensity, activation, collision energy
Returns chromatograms: id, index, type, time array and unit, intensity array
Expands referenceableParamGroupRef where it is used and reports an unknown group
Raises MzMLError for MS-Numpress or any other compression except zlib, and for a missing or unsupported array type, data type or compression term
Raises MzMLError for a decoded length that does not match defaultArrayLength or arrayLength, a wrong encodedLength, and invalid base64 or zlib data
Raises MzMLError for malformed XML and for a document that is not mzML
The command line prints a summary of each file and exits with status 1 when a file cannot be read
Reports malformed XML and missing required top-level elements (MZV001-MZV002)
Reports unresolved cvRef / unitCvRef / param group / instrument configuration / data processing references (MZV003-MZV006)
Reports wrong list counts, non-consecutive indices and duplicate ids (MZV010-MZV012)
Reports array length, decoding, encodedLength and missing-array problems (MZV020-MZV024)
Reports spectrum content problems: no centroid/profile term, decreasing m/z, negative intensities, no MS level, MSn without precursor (MZV030-MZV034)
Reports chromatogram length mismatches and decreasing time (MZV040-MZV041)
Verifies indexed files: offsets, indexListOffset, SHA-1 checksum and index coverage (MZV050-MZV053)
Each invalid sample yields exactly its documented finding and the valid samples yield none
The command line exits with status 1 on any error and --strict turns warnings into errors
TIC is the sum of all intensities of each MS1 spectrum
BPC is the largest intensity of each MS1 spectrum with the m/z of that peak
XIC sums the intensities inside a centre +/- tolerance window in ppm or Da, bounds included
Only MS1 spectra contribute; other spectra are skipped and counted
Times keep the unit of the file; mixed units in one file are an error
The computed TIC is compared with the declared TIC chromatogram and per-spectrum total ion current values, and differences are reported
Writes all traces as CSV with one row per MS1 spectrum
Draws a trace as an SVG line plot with labelled axes and units, identical on every run
The command line prints a summary with the TIC cross-check and writes CSV and SVG on request
Writes plain mzML and indexedmzML with correct byte offsets, indexListOffset and SHA-1 checksum
What it writes reads back to the same values (64-bit exact, 32-bit to float32 precision) for every encoding combination
Every file it writes passes mzml_validator.py --strict with no findings
Refuses input that would make an invalid or ambiguous file with ValueError
Uses generic PSI-MS metadata terms only
The sample generators are deterministic: the same seed gives the same files (decoded values for zlib files)
The caffeine [M+H]+ isotope pattern is computed from natural abundances (m/z 195.0877, M+1 about 10.3 %)
Sample files use generic instrument metadata only and stay small
The matrix generator maps test markers to JUnit results, lists requirements without tests and rejects unknown requirement ids
